{{Short description|Type of large cardinal number}}
In [[set theory]], a '''Rowbottom cardinal''', introduced by [[Frederick Rowbottom]],{{sfnp|Rowbottom|1971}} is a certain kind of [[large cardinal]] number.

An [[uncountable set|uncountable]] [[cardinal number]] <math>\kappa</math> is said to be '''''{{math|λ}}-Rowbottom''''' if for every function <math>f:[\kappa]^{<\omega}\to\lambda</math> (where <math>\lambda < \kappa</math>) there is a set <math>H</math> of order type <math>\kappa</math> that is quasi-[[Homogeneous (large cardinal property)|homogeneous]] for <math>f</math>, i.e., for every <math>n</math>, the <math>f</math>-image of the set of <math>n</math>-element subsets of <math>H</math> has <math><\lambda</math> elements. <math>\kappa</math> is simply '''''Rowbottom''''' if it is '''''{{math|ω<sub>1</sub>}}-Rowbottom'''''.

Every [[Ramsey cardinal]] is Rowbottom, and every Rowbottom cardinal is [[Jónsson cardinal|Jónsson]]. By a theorem of Kleinberg, the theories ZFC + “there is a Rowbottom cardinal” and ZFC + “there is a Jónsson cardinal” are equiconsistent.

In general, Rowbottom cardinals need not be [[large cardinal]]s in the usual sense: Rowbottom cardinals could be [[singular cardinal|singular]]. It is an open question whether ZFC + “<math>\aleph_{\omega}</math> is Rowbottom” is consistent. If it is, it has much higher consistency strength than the existence of a Rowbottom cardinal. The [[axiom of determinacy]] does imply that <math>\aleph_{\omega}</math> is Rowbottom (but contradicts the [[axiom of choice]]).
